n48d47bb3ddd2: by Lijuan Zhang This paper addresses the inherent trade off between rapid convergence and high‑precision disturbance rejection in intelligent vehicle motion control under severe nonlinearities, parametric uncertainties, and time varying external perturbations. A composite finite‑time robust control strategy is proposed by synergistically integrating a nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode (NFTSM) surface, radial basis function neural networks (RBFNN), and a finite time disturbance observer (FTDO). The NFTSM guarantees singularity free finite time convergence of the tracking errors. The RBFNN approximates the slowly varying unknown dynamics, while the FTDO compensates online for the neural approximation residual and fast varying disturbances in a cascaded “coarse to fine” manner. Lyapunov-based Extensive co‑simulations with MATLAB/Simulink, conducted under double lane change and sinusoidal path scenarios with simultaneous road friction drops and stochastic lateral wind gusts, demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms conventional nonsingular terminal sliding mode control and disturbance observer based sliding mode control in terms of tracking accuracy, convergence speed, and chattering suppression.
nb01ed978fd30: Background Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of blindness in working-age populations. Astrocyte senescence is highly prevalent in DR, but the underlying regulatory mechanism remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the role of the HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis in regulating retinal astrocyte senescence and endothelial function in DR. Methods Mouse retinal astrocytes were exposed to high glucose (30 mM) to mimic diabetic conditions. Senescence was evaluated by β-galactosidase staining. Signaling pathways were manipulated using HIF-1α inhibitor (PX-478), PPAR-γ inhibitor (T0070907), SIRT1 agonist (SRT2104), and autophagy inhibitor (3-MA). Protein and mRNA levels of key factors were detected by Western blot and RT-qPCR. Astrocytes and retinal microvascular endothelial cells were co-cultured in Transwell systems to assess paracrine regulation on endothelial migration, proliferation, and apoptosis. Results High glucose induced astrocyte senescence, inflammatory activation, and downregulation of GDNF and NRTN, accompanied by elevated HIF-1α and PPAR-γ, and reduced SIRT1 expression and autophagy activity. Inhibiting HIF-1α or activating SIRT1 attenuated senescence, apoptosis, and inflammation, restored autophagy, and upregulated GDNF/NRTN secretion. HIF-1α negatively regulated SIRT1 expression via PPAR-γ. Senescent astrocytes impaired endothelial function through reduced GDNF/NRTN; overexpression of GDNF or NRTN in astrocytes preserved endothelial migration and proliferation, and inhibited apoptosis. Conclusion HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis mediates high glucose-induced astrocyte senescence via autophagy dysfunction. Senescent astrocytes disrupt retinal endothelial homeostasis by reducing GDNF/NRTN secretion. Targeting this axis may represent a novel neurovascular protective therapeutic strategy for DR.
n351a601e0d7e: Background HIV-related stigma remains a significant barrier to prevention and treatment efforts in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. This study assessed HIV knowledge and stigmatizing attitudes among United Arab Emirates (UAE) residents. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted across the UAE between January and March 2025. A total of 1,211 eligible adult residents were recruited through convenience sampling. Demographic analyses included all 1,211 participants, while HIV knowledge and stigma analyses included 1,171 participants with analyzable outcome data. The questionnaire assessed demographics, HIV transmission knowledge, and stigmatizing attitudes using the Stigmatizing Attitudes Towards People Living with HIV/AIDS Scale (SAT-PLWHA-S). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, bivariate analyses, and multiple linear regression. Results Among the 1,211 participants included in the study, 1,171 contributed analyzable data to the HIV knowledge and stigma analyses. While 96.4% had heard of HIV/AIDS and demonstrated moderately high transmission knowledge (mean score: 75.5%), significant misconceptions persisted, particularly regarding condom effectiveness (60.5% overestimated risk). Strong stigmatizing attitudes emerged, especially regarding criminalization of transmission (79.6% support) and moralistic views. Higher knowledge correlated with less stigma (r = 0.347, p < 0.001), though nationality, language preference, and knowing someone with HIV were stronger predictors. Only 6.2% knew someone with HIV. Conclusions Despite adequate basic knowledge, significant HIV-related stigma persists in the UAE, driven by cultural and moral perspectives. Comprehensive interventions combining education, contact-based strategies, and policy reform are needed to reduce stigma and improve HIV prevention outcomes.
n837c38b621f3: Background Vaginal fistula (VF), particularly vesicovaginal fistula (VVF), remains a significant reproductive health challenge in many low-resource settings, including the Kpandai District of Ghana. Despite its profound physical and psychosocial impact, the lived experiences of affected women in rural districts remain under-documented. Aim This study explored the lived experiences of women diagnosed with vesicovaginal fistula in the Kpandai District of Ghana, focusing on their physical, emotional, and social challenges, as well as coping strategies. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using in-depth interviews with ten women with clinically confirmed VVF. Participants were initially identified through a district health facility and subsequently recruited using a combination of purposive and snowball sampling techniques. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically. Results Prolonged and obstructed labour—often occurring at home—emerged as the primary reported cause of VVF. Cultural beliefs, gender-based decision-making dynamics, limited access to healthcare, and financial constraints were key barriers to timely medical intervention. Consequences included persistent urinary incontinence, social stigma, emotional trauma, marital dissolution (reported by eight participants), loss of livelihood, and social isolation. Coping strategies included frequent washing, use of absorbent materials, and reliance on perfumes or herbal remedies. Conclusions Vesicovaginal fistula remains a devastating yet largely preventable condition in rural Ghana. The findings highlight the need to strengthen maternal health services, improve timely referral systems, and integrate psychosocial support within community-based care frameworks.
n763d095e7633: Expanding access to a broad range of contraceptive methods is critical for reducing unintended pregnancies and improving reproductive health. This study evaluates the introduction of subdermal contraceptive implants in the selected areas of Honduras and Chiapas, Mexico, in the context of the Salud Mesoamérica Initiative, a results-based financing program focused on disadvantaged populations. Data were obtained from household surveys conducted between 2012 and 2022 among women aged 15–49 years in selected intervention and comparison municipalities in Chiapas, Mexico, and Honduras, using a two-stage sampling design. Indicators included contraceptive prevalence rates, reasons for method switching, and adoption by sociodemographic characteristics. Findings show a substantial increase in implant use in both settings over time. In the selected areas of Honduras, implant uptake increased gradually, reaching 7.9% in the 2022 SMI household survey, while in the selected areas of Chiapas use rose to 7.2%. Younger women aged 20–29 years and those with full literacy exhibited the highest adoption rates. In the selected areas of Chiapas and Honduras, implants most often replaced non-modern and short-acting hormonal methods, suggesting successful integration into the existing method mix. Variations in adoption across sociodemographic subgroups highlight persistent inequities. The results underscore the potential of subdermal implants to expand access to long-acting reversible contraception in resource-limited settings. To sustain and enhance this progress, strategies must address sociocultural and structural barriers, ensuring equitable access across all population groups and mitigating service disruptions. These findings may inform future strategies to expand informed contraceptive choice in similar resource-limited settings; their effects on reproductive health outcomes require further evaluation.
n4e2d55aa3a66: Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of mortality and long-term neurological disability worldwide. Secondary injury mechanisms, particularly neuroinflammation, play a key role in determining neurological outcomes after the initial trauma. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway has recently been identified as a mediator of innate immune activation following brain injury. Activation of this pathway promotes microglial activation and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, contributing to neuronal damage and impaired recovery. Pharmacological inhibition of the cGAS-STING signaling pathway has therefore emerged as a promising neuroprotective strategy in experimental TBI models. However, the available preclinical evidence has not yet been systematically synthesized. Methods A systematic literature search was performed across MEDLINE, EMBASE and Web of Science without language or publication date restrictions. Titles and abstracts were screened independently by two reviewers, followed by independent full-text eligibility assessment. Data extraction was initiated subsequently and will be completed independently by two reviewers. Eligible studies will include in vivo animal models of TBI investigating direct or indirect pharmacological inhibition of the cGAS-STING pathway administered after injury, compared with vehicle-treated or untreated controls. The primary outcome will be quantitative measures of microglial activation within the first 72 hours post-injury, preferentially assessed using Iba1-positive cell density or percentage-stained area. Secondary outcomes will include astrocytic reactivity, cytokine expression (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6), lesion volume and neurological functional recovery. Risk of bias will be assessed using the SYRCLE tool. When appropriate, pooled effect sizes will be calculated using random-effects meta-analysis. Heterogeneity, publication bias and certainty of evidence will also be evaluated. Discussion This systematic review and meta-analysis will help clarify the magnitude and consistency of therapeutic effects and inform the translational potential of this strategy while identifying methodological limitations that may guide future experimental and clinical research. Systematic review registration PROSPERO CRD420261367166.
n6eca3f37181f: by Mathilda C. Mennen, Michael Z. Zulu, Koketso C. Mabatha, Richard Baguma, Sango Skelem, Nandipha N. Mbundwini, Olukayode O. Aremu, Marguerite Adriaanse, Daphne van Dijk, Preyanka Pillay, Sam Africa, Erika Jones, Mashiko Setshedi, Adrian Brink, Wendy A. Burgers, Ntobeko A. B. Ntusi Background Hypertension is a leading contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with poor control in low- and middle-income countries. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) has been associated with hypertension through inflammatory, endothelial, metabolic and immune pathways, but data from sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in resistant hypertension, are limited. Methods This cross-sectional observational study will enrol 200 adults aged ≥18 at a tertiary academic hospital in Cape Town, South Africa: 80 with resistant hypertension, 80 with non-resistant hypertension and 40 with normotension. Participants will undergo standardised clinical assessment, blood pressure measurement, and collection of blood, urine and saliva. H. pylori exposure will be assessed using the Pylori DuoTect® point-of-care assay, which detects antibodies to CagA and FliD. Laboratory analyses will include lipid profile, inflammatory and nitric oxide-related markers, homocysteine, insulin indices, complete blood count, ghrelin, multiplex cytokine profiling and flow cytometric immunophenotyping. PAXgene® blood RNA samples will be retained for future exploratory analyses. Saliva will undergo exploratory H. pylori antigen testing using CerTest® kits, which are validated for stool rather than saliva. Saliva analysis will be exploratory, and results will not define the primary H. pylori exposure variable. Remaining saliva will be kept for potential future oral microbiome analyses not defined in this protocol. Multivariable logistic regression will evaluate associations between H. pylori exposure and hypertension phenotype, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates. Discussion To our knowledge, this will be the first African study to integrate point-of-care H. pylori serology with detailed clinical, inflammatory, metabolic, and immunological profiling across resistant hypertension, non-resistant hypertension and normotension. Findings may clarify biological pathways linking H. pylori exposure to blood pressure dysregulation and inform future mechanistic and interventional studies.
n5e50ddec0859: Introduction Rapid industrialization in Bangladesh, especially in Gazipur District, has raised concern over heavy metal contamination of soil and water and the associated health risks to nearby residents. This study compared the concentration, spatial distribution, probable sources, and non-carcinogenic health risk of five heavy metals (Hg, Ni, Mn, Zn, and Co) in soil and water in the Turag River areas in Gazipur District. Methods Soil and water samples were collected from 18 sites in the Turag River (including both industrial and non-industrial zones) and analyzed for five heavy metal concentrations (Hg, Ni, Mn, Zn, and Co) using inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Statistical analyses included principal component analysis (PCA), hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), and Pearson correlation analysis, while non-carcinogenic human health risks were evaluated using the USEPA-based chronic daily intake (CDI), hazard quotient (HQ), and hazard index (HI) models for both adults and children. Results Mean soil metal concentrations followed the order Mn > Zn > Ni > Co > Hg in both zones, with markedly higher and more spatially concentrated Ni and Zn levels in the industrial zone near the Turag River areas. Spatial mapping, PCA, HCA, and correlation analyses consistently suggested a common anthropogenic influence on soil and water contamination in the industrial zone, with the strongest spatial concentrations observed near its northern boundary, compared with patterns consistent with multiple diffuse influences in the non-industrial zone. The modeled soil CDI values were generally higher for children than adults. Soil-based screening estimates indicated potential non-carcinogenic concern for children, including an Ni HQ of 1.66 in the industrial zone and cumulative hazard index values above the screening benchmark of 1 for children in both the industrial (HI = 2.32) and non-industrial (HI = 1.31) zones, while all modeled HQ and HI values for water remained below the screening benchmark of 1. Conclusion These soil-based screening estimates suggest potential non-carcinogenic concern for children, particularly regarding Ni in the industrial zone, but are based on the < 0.5 mm fraction of soil collected at 15–20 cm depth and may not represent actual exposure to ground-surface soil or airborne particles. The study highlighted the need for targeted control of potential industrial sources and child-focused environmental health monitoring in industrializing peri-urban districts of Bangladesh.
n052bdf670091: Background Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) are novel nicotine products and evidence on how features of ONP packaging affect product engagement, perceptions, use intentions, and behavior is limited. Objectives We outline the protocol for a randomized trial examining how nicotine concentration and nicotine source claims affect engagement with ONP packaging using psychophysiological measures, self-reported ONP perceptions and use intentions, and ONP trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06192316). Methods Between 2024 and 2027, we will recruit 450 participants, comprised of: 150 young adults ages 18–24 who are susceptible but do not use tobacco; 150 young adults ages 18–24 who use tobacco; and 150 adults ages 25–65 who use tobacco. Participants complete procedures at an in-person laboratory visit. During the visit, participants complete pre-exposure self-report measures and are randomized between subjects to one of nine conditions in a 3 (Nicotine Concentration: None, Low, or High) x 3 (Nicotine Source Claim: None, Tobacco Free, or Synthetic) design. Within conditions, participants view 16 ONP pack images, in random order, reflecting different ONP brands and flavors. During exposure, we collect psychophysiological measures including heart rate, skin conductance, and visual attention. After exposure, participants complete self-report measures of ONP perceptions and use intentions, and a timed behavioral task where they are presented with ONP packages corresponding to their randomized condition and brands and flavors shown in the stimuli. Participants can try one of the products, and ONP trial is the behavioral outcome of interest. However, the packages do not contain ONPs; they contain commercially available pouches with food grade ingredients. At visit conclusion, participants are de-briefed and receive their incentive for participating. Conclusions This project will generate evidence on the effects of nicotine concentration and source claims on ONP packaging in young adults who are not using but susceptible to tobacco, young adults using tobacco, and adults using tobacco to inform potential regulations.
n292b97e57814: Objective The global target to halve the prevalence of anemia by 2025 has not been met. New strategies are needed. This systematic review examined the effect of tranexamic acid on anemia, menstrual health and wellbeing in women of reproductive age. Methods We searched six databases from inception to 30 August 2025 and reference lists of seven related reviews. We included randomized trials comparing the effects of tranexamic acid with placebo or standard care on uterine bleeding. Eligible participants had normal menstrual bleeding or any type of non-pregnant abnormal uterine bleeding. Outcomes included hemoglobin concentration and anemia prevalence as the primary outcome, estimated blood loss, quality of life, thromboembolic events, and other adverse events. We conducted meta-analyses and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) and the certainty of evidence. Results We included 17 trials in the review and 15 in the meta-analyses. None of the trials reported adequate data on hemoglobin concentration. For the anemia outcome, only one small trial contributed data (risk ratio 0.15, 95% confidence interval 0.01 to 2.74, very low certainty). Meta-analyses of secondary outcomes showed that tranexamic acid reduced objectively measured menstrual blood loss among women with heavy menstrual bleeding (6 trials, mean difference −47.0 milliliters, 95% confidence interval −56.6 to −37.4, I2 = 13%, moderate certainty) and in women with intrauterine devices (3 trials, mean difference −41.6 milliliters, 95% confidence interval −52.2 to −30.9, I2 = 64%, low certainty) and improved quality of life in women with heavy menstrual bleeding (2 trials, mean difference 0.5, 95% confidence interval 0.4 to 0.7, I2 = 0%, moderate certainty). The risk of nausea or vomiting was similar between groups (4 trials, risk ratio 1.0, 95% confidence interval 0.6 to 1.8, I2 = 0%, moderate certainty). Certainty of evidence for other outcomes ranged from very low to low, including for thromboembolic events, with only one event reported in the control arm of one trial. Conclusions Tranexamic acid appears to reduce menstrual blood loss, but its impact on anemia is unclear. High-quality randomized trials of TXA for menstruating women with anemia are needed.
na2c80f3898eb: This study investigated the relationship between muscle strength and tennis performance, assessed using the International Tennis Number (ITN) on-court test, operationalized as point-based outcomes (total points and subcomponent points), in young female tennis players aged under 12 (U12) and under 14 (U14). Thirty-three players underwent a comprehensive evaluation including ITN testing, general strength tests (handgrip strength, flexed arm hang, and tennis-ball throw), isometric upper-limb muscle strength, and sense of force assessment. Results demonstrated significantly higher ITN scores and muscle strength in the U14 group, with differences largely attributable to body size and training experience. Correlation analyses revealed age-specific patterns: in U12 players, ITN scores were associated primarily with general strength measures, whereas in U14 players, they were more strongly linked to joint-specific upper-limb strength and neuromuscular characteristics. Sense of force did not differ between groups, though correlations with ITN varied depending on age and joint function. These findings suggest that, in this sample, performance in younger players was more closely associated with general strength measures, whereas in older players it was more closely associated with joint-specific upper-limb strength.
n2c32a8ed42d1: Intracranial hypertension is a frequent complication of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVT), posing a risk for permanent visual impairment. However, long-term visual outcomes have not been systematically assessed using objective neuro-ophthalmic measures. We retrospectively evaluated consecutive adults presenting to a single-center tertiary intracranial hypertension clinic between 2019 and 2025 with intracranial hypertension following CVT. Visual outcomes were assessed using best-corrected visual acuity, automated perimetry, and optical coherence tomography measuring global peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. Headache phenotype and medication overuse were documented. Nineteen patients (11 female; mean age 33.4 ± 12.1 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 3.4 ± 2.4 years after diagnosis of CVT-related intracranial hypertension. The transverse sinus was involved in 78.9% of cases, and complete or near-complete recanalization was achieved in 68.4%. Although visual acuity remained normal in most patients (84.2%), 26.3% had severe visual field loss and 15.8% showed retinal nerve fiber layer thinning. Headache persisted in 94.7%, most commonly as tension-type headache (63.2%), and 26.3% fulfilled criteria for medication overuse headache. Despite generally preserved visual acuity, substantial visual field deficits and persistent headache were common in CVT-related intracranial hypertension. These findings support routine neuro-ophthalmic follow-up to facilitate early detection of visual deterioration in CVT-related intracranial hypertension. As this cohort was drawn from a specialized tertiary referral clinic, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than representative of the broader CVT population.
na36444cc882f: This study examines whether temporal ordering between X and online news varies across first-level issue and second-level attribute agendas in Türkiye’s polarized media environment. The analysis draws on 448,664 X posts and 10,357 articles from 19 mainstream online news outlets collected during the 31-day period preceding and including the 31 March 2024 Istanbul local election. Using 12-hour AM/PM windows, we conducted 122 cross-lagged panel analyses—62 same-day AM → PM and 60 overnight PM→next-day AM panels across the two agenda levels—comparing issue- and attribute-indicator frequency profiles. First-level issue agendas were strongly synchronized, with correlations often approaching or exceeding r = .90, whereas second-level attribute relationships were weaker and less consistent. At the first level, morning online news issue salience more often preceded later X issue salience within same-day transitions, whereas evening X issue salience more often preceded the following morning’s online news issue salience across overnight transitions. Most first-level cross-lagged correlations exceeded their Rozelle–Campbell (RCb) baselines, while second-level coefficients did so less consistently. These findings indicate that agenda leadership in a hybrid media system is temporally contingent and level-specific rather than static. The observed patterns represent temporally ordered associations and should not be interpreted as evidence of direct causal influence.
n3db3869c5a76: The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.
nd702f2f76044: Chromosomal inversions are an important class of genetic variation that link multiple alleles together into a single inherited block that can have important effects on fitness. To study the role of large inversions in the massive evolutionary radiation of Lake Malawi cichlids, we used long-read technologies to identify four single and two tandem inversions that span half of each respective chromosome, and which together encompass over 10% of the genome. Each inversion is fixed in one of the two states within the seven major ecogroups, suggesting they played a role in the separation of the major lake lineages into specific lake habitats. One exception is within the benthic sub-radiation, where both inverted and non-inverted alleles continue to segregate within the group. The evolutionary histories of three of the six inversions suggest they transferred from the pelagic Diplotaxodon group into benthic ancestors at the time the benthic sub-radiation was seeded. The remaining three inversions are found in a subset of benthic species living in deep waters. We show that some of these inversions are linked to XY sex-determination systems but are also likely limited to a subset of total lake species. Our work suggests that inversions have been under both sexual and natural selection in Lake Malawi cichlids and that they will be important to understanding how this adaptive radiation evolved.
nb81a75e81f0b: Male Drosophila courtship behavior is a key model for studying temporal decision-making. While courtship index (CI) is widely used to quantify mating activity, other timing metrics like courtship latency, copulation latency (CL), and mating duration (MD) remain understudied. Traditional methods for quantifying these behaviors are often labor-intensive and prone to human error. In this study, we present a protocol combining a modular chamber system and automated software (DrosoMating) to quantify six key timing metrics during male courtship. Our image-based video analysis enables precise identification of courtship and copulation events, as well as quantification of their timing and duration under controlled conditions. Validation shows <0.05% error rates and 98–99% agreement with manual scoring for CL, CI, and MD. The protocol supports genetic and neural circuit manipulations, detecting subtle genetic, social, and environmental behavioral variations. By minimizing manual effort and standardizing data collection, this approach facilitates scalable, reproducible studies on adaptive trade-offs, learning, and neural mechanisms in mating behavior. This method streamlines timing analysis in male courtship, offering reproducible metrics for behavioral genetics.
n7c62b94c98b9: Epithelial cells undergo epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) during migration and regain their epithelial phenotype in the post-migration phase (mesenchymal–epithelial transition [MET]). We established an experimental system that reproduces a three-compartment epithelial structure comprising the original epithelium, its EMT state, and its MET state. Keratinocytes (KCs), skin epithelial cells, placed on a microporous membrane, migrated through 3.0 µm or larger micropores. The 3.0-µm-pored membrane induced an epithelial structure with three distinct states: stratified KCs above the membrane, KCs showing EMT within the micropores, and a new stratified epithelium under the membrane. The membrane with larger micropores failed to maintain the three-compartment epithelial structure. Live imaging revealed that KCs moved in an oscillatory manner, with actin-rich filopodia-like structures extending into and out of the 3.0 µm micropores, while the cells migrated unidirectionally into larger micropores. Piezo1 and keratin 6 were identified as negative modulators of KC entry into and exit from the 3.0 µm micropores. These results demonstrate that non-cancerous epithelial cells migrate through confined spaces in an oscillatory manner, which might contribute to the formation of a three-compartment epithelial structure that recapitulates key aspects of wound healing.
n2217a2c6fa0a: A coordinated response to stress is crucial for promoting the short- and long-term health of an organism. The perception of stress, frequently through the nervous system, can lead to physiological changes that are fundamental to maintaining homeostasis. Activating the response to low oxygen, or hypoxia, extends healthspan and lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. However, despite some positive impacts, negative effects of the hypoxic response in specific tissues prevent translation of their benefits in mammals. Thus, it is imperative to identify which components of this response promote longevity. Here, we interrogate the cell-nonautonomous signaling pathway downstream of genetic activation of the hypoxic response. We find that HIF-1-mediated signaling in ADF serotonergic neurons is both necessary and sufficient for lifespan extension. Signaling through the serotonin receptor SER-7 in the GABAergic RIS interneurons is necessary in this process. Our findings also highlight the involvement of additional neural signaling molecules, including the neurotransmitters tyramine and GABA, and the neuropeptide NLP-17, in mediating longevity effects. Finally, we demonstrate that oxygen- and carbon-dioxide-sensing neurons act downstream of HIF-1 in this circuit. Together, these insights demonstrate a circuit for how genetic induction of the hypoxic response cell-nonautonomously modifies aging and suggests valuable targets for modulating aging in mammals.
n1f5bab73c569: The ability to determine how much the environment can be controlled through our actions has long been viewed as fundamental to adaptive behavior. While traditional accounts treat controllability as a fixed property of the environment, we argue that real-world controllability often depends on the effort, time, and money we are able and willing to invest. In such cases, controllability can be said to be elastic to invested resources. Here, we propose that inferring this elasticity is essential for efficient resource allocation, and thus, elasticity misestimations result in maladaptive behavior. To test this hypothesis, we developed a novel treasure hunt game where participants encountered environments with varying degrees of controllability and elasticity. Across two pre-registered studies (N=514), we first demonstrate that people infer elasticity and adapt their resource allocation accordingly. We then present a computational model that explains how people make this inference and identify individual elasticity biases that lead to suboptimal resource allocation. Finally, we show that overestimation of elasticity is associated with elevated psychopathology involving an impaired sense of control. These findings establish the elasticity of control as a distinct cognitive construct guiding adaptive behavior and a computational marker for control-related maladaptive behavior.
n1086c8226d15: Scope taking is one of the most characteristic, distinctive, and ubiquitous phenomena in natural language. When an expression takes scope, it combines with surrounding material as its semantic argument. For instance, in Amy gave everyone a book , the semantic argument of everyone is an abstraction over the entire rest of the sentence, namely, λ x . Amy gave x a book , the property an individual has if Amy gave that individual a book. This ability to operate on surrounding context dramatically enriches (and complicates) the ways that meanings can be expressed. Although there are many formal theories of scope taking, Quantifier Raising—often thought of as a covert (silent) version of overt syntactic movement—is by far the dominant approach. There are many constraints on the availability of scope taking that depend on the identity of the scope taker as well as on its surrounding context.
nd217c2aa324d: A speech sample can be morphed from one voice to another by computing a sufficiently detailed time-frequency parameterization of the signal, optionally decomposing it into speaker-dependent and speaker-independent signal components, editing the parameterization or signal components, and then generating a speech signal based on the edited parameterization. Fine-grained control of time-frequency parameters has found applications in the scientific study of speech perception and in artistic applications such as voiceover and music. Coarse-grained control of speaker identity, emotion, and second-language accent have been applied to various tasks, including the training of speech recognizers and speaker anonymization.
n4dbe9ebfb917: Singular they is valuable to psycholinguistic research because it has a long-standing usage in English that is currently undergoing changes, both in how often it is used and in what conditions. As a result, singular they is an informative testing ground for the cognitive mechanisms behind language change, which include both top-down intentional change and implicit learning and adaptation. Singular they is also an unusually socially salient function word that provides opportunities to examine how automatic psycholinguistic processes intersect with sociolinguistic issues like gender-fair language, linguistic prescriptivism, and the emerging use of they as a personal pronoun. Developments in the use of singular they are linked to broader shifts in concepts of gender. We suggest that there are two main varieties of singular they that currently differ in acceptability and processing characteristics. Psycholinguistic research shows that singular they is viewed as more acceptable and used more easily within a supportive context that helps to make the pronoun pragmatically appropriate.
n94a2ed0497d5: Biomass-burning organic aerosol (BBOA) is a major component of atmospheric particulate matter and is expected to become increasingly important as wildfire activity increases. The viscosity and phase state of BBOA influence its climate and health impacts. This review summarizes current understanding of the viscosity and phase state of BBOA. Measurements show that the viscosity of unaged primary BBOA spans more than ten orders of magnitude, from liquid-like particles to glassy solids, depending on fuel type, combustion conditions, burn stage, and relative humidity. Aging by evaporation, OH oxidation, UV irradiation, and secondary aerosol formation can increase viscosity by several orders of magnitude. Field measurements indicate that atmospheric BBOA is often more viscous than unaged laboratory BBOA. Laboratory measurements further suggest that aged BBOA commonly exists in highly viscous or glassy states in the free troposphere and may exhibit mixing times exceeding one hour. We also highlight future research directions.
n9ee3a97c4b4c: Automated visual inspection of aero-engine blades is central to aviation safety, yet it is challenged by damage that is small and low-contrast against a strongly textured metal surface, and by the need for models that are light enough for edge deployment. This paper presents a lightweight vision-based framework for automated blade damage inspection. Rather than assembling independent detection modules, the framework is organized as a three-stage inspection pipeline: (1) a multi-scale feature-discrimination stage (MSBlock) captures defects across a wide size range at negligible computational cost; (2) a texture-suppression stage (TSA) filters high-frequency machining-background noise through product-based channel–spatial attention, exposing genuine defects; and (3) an efficient-prediction stage (Detect_Efficient) fuses cross-scale features and recalibrates confidence with roughly half the parameters of a standard head. On a self-built engine-blade dataset, the framework improves recall, F1-score, and mAP@0.5 by 4.8, 1.9, and 0.8 percentage points over YOLOv11n (reaching 92.0%, 91.6%, and 94.2%), while cutting parameters and computation by 50.0% and 58.7% and reaching 527 FPS. It also outperforms YOLOv8n, YOLOv9t, and YOLOv10n in recall and F1-score, confirming its suitability for real-time edge-based blade inspection.
n1b8d1c3473cc: Dynamics of messenger ribonucleic acids (mRNAs) and the complexes with associated proteins (RNPs), also known as RNA granules, provide post-transcriptional control of gene expression. This regulation is crucial for cell-type diversity and activity-dependent plasticity of the mammalian central nervous system (CNS). However, elucidating the physiological significance of RNA granules has been hampered by technical difficulties to probe them in live brain. Here, we describe a novel method to visualize RNA granules in native CNS tissues of mouse. To amplify the fluorescence signal from single mRNAs incorporating MS2 stem loops, MS2 capsid protein (MCP) was conjugated with 4 tandem superfolder green fluorescent proteins (sfGFPs). Using MCP-4 × sfGFP, significantly more RNPs could be detected in the fresh acute brain slices than with MCP-GFP. Amplified MS2 signal could visualize Actb mRNAs in specific cells, either driven by promoter or via Cre-dependent expression, revealing remarkably distinct localization and movements of RNPs across different CNS cell types, including neurons and glial cells. The highly sensitive live-tissue RNA imaging could be useful for investigating the regulation of the dynamics of RNA granules in the native niche, ultimately in naive and diseased animal models.
n34f519c515c1: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health problem, and early detection is important for reducing complications and improving treatment. Machine learning has shown strong potential for CKD prediction, but many existing studies rely on single datasets, face severe class imbalance, and provide limited interpretability. These challenges reduce model reliability and make cross-dataset use in real clinical settings more difficult. Therefore, this study aimed to develop an interpretable and adaptable machine learning framework for CKD risk prediction across different datasets. The proposed hybrid explainable machine learning (HXAI-ML) framework used two public CKD datasets: the UCI CKD Risk Factor Prediction dataset as the source dataset and the Kaggle CKD dataset as the target dataset. After preprocessing, label binarization, imputation, and standard scaling, seven balancing methods and six classifiers were evaluated. A target adaptation setting was applied by using 10% of the target dataset for calibration and 90% for blind testing. SHAP, LIME, and Permutation Importance Analysis were used to explain the model predictions. Among all tested combinations, RO + TL + ETC achieved the highest overall accuracy among the evaluated target-domain adaptation configurations and was therefore selected as the primary model under the accuracy-based selection criterion. On the 1,494-sample blind holdout it obtained 91.97% accuracy, 92.24% precision, 99.64% recall, 95.80% F1-score, and 67.52% ROC-AUC. However, its specificity of 5.74% and balanced accuracy of 52.69% indicate substantial class-wise imbalance in predictive performance. The findings demonstrate the methodological feasibility of cross-dataset target-domain adaptation and explainable machine learning under limited target-domain data. However, the relatively low ROC-AUC values and low specificity for the non-CKD class indicate limited discriminative ability. Therefore, the proposed framework should be regarded as an exploratory cross-dataset evaluation rather than a clinically deployable screening or decision-support system.
ndad650d96ee9: Fresh vegetables consumed raw are a recognized but underappreciated vehicle for foodborne pathogens and antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) bacteria, yet data on AMR determinants in fresh produce remain scarce for West Africa. This cross-sectional study characterized the prevalence of Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp. in 300 fresh vegetable samples from farms, markets, restaurants, and supermarkets in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, along with their antimicrobial resistance profiles, selected β-lactamase genes, and associated food-handling risk factors. E. coli was detected in 63.0% of samples (95% CI: 57.4–68.3%) and Salmonella spp. in 10.0% (95% CI: 6.9–13.9%). Prevalence did not differ significantly by season for either species (E. coli: 61.3% dry season vs 64.7% rainy season, χ²(1) = 0.36, p = 0.55; Salmonella: 8.0% vs 12.0%, χ²(1) = 1.33, p = 0.25). Per-agent resistance rates were likewise broadly similar between seasons for both species (e.g., Salmonella tetracycline resistance 23.3% dry vs 26.7% rainy). Salmonella isolates showed higher resistance for several individual agents than E. coli isolates, most notably tetracycline (25.0% vs 15.3%) and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (21.7% vs 12.8%; see Table 1). Multidrug resistance (non-susceptibility to ≥ 3 antimicrobial classes) was observed in 60% of resistant Salmonella isolates. Among eight resistant isolates screened by multiplex polymerase chain reaction (four E. coli and four Salmonella, selected to represent the range of resistance phenotypes observed), blaTEM was detected in 100% (8/8), blaOXA in 50.0% (4/8), and blaCTX-M in 50.0% (4/8), with co-occurrence of all three genes in 37.5% (3/8) of isolates. The detection of the extended-spectrum β-lactamase-associated blaCTX-M gene provides new surveillance data on vegetable-associated bacteria in Burkina Faso, an environmental compartment not previously included in national AMR monitoring. Risky food-handling practices were widespread: 98% of vendors stored vegetables at ambient temperature, 85% applied no disinfection, and 80% of settings presented cross-contamination risk with raw meat. A screening-level model yielded an indicative 2.0% exposure-risk estimate for antibiotic-resistant Salmonella per raw salad serving; this is a screening-level indicator rather than a confirmed infection probability (see Methods). A HACCP-based control framework with five critical control points is proposed as a preliminary, field-validation-pending tool. These findings support the integration of fresh produce into One Health antimicrobial resistance surveillance strategies in West Africa.
n865bc8aa06e3: Coronaviruses are responsible for diseases ranging from mild respiratory symptoms to severe infections such as COVID-19. Despite the availability of vaccines and therapeutic agents, the emergence of new variants and drug-resistant strains highlights the need for additional antiviral strategies. In this study, Rumex crispus was investigated as a potential source of antiviral compounds. The ethanol (EtOH) extract of R. crispus roots was prepared and subsequently fractionated into n-hexane (n-hex), ethyl acetate (EA), and aqueous fractions. Among these, the n-hexane and EA fractions exhibited significant antiviral activity against human coronavirus OC43, as demonstrated by Western blot, qRT-PCR, and plaque assays. Chemical analysis of the extract by HPLC led to the identification of epicatechin, naphthalene derivatives, and anthraquinones. Notably, emodin, an anthraquinone, showed pronounced antiviral activity, and was found to be enriched in the active n-hexane and EA fractions. These findings suggest that emodin may contribute to the antiviral activity of R. crispus extract, although the potential involvement of other bioactive constituents cannot be excluded.
n1486a7f89996: Background Clinical supervision is regarded as essential for nurse managers in diverse healthcare settings to enhance nurse satisfaction, competence, and retention, leading to improved nursing care quality. The study aimed to explore and describe nurse managers’ support provided to registered nurses during clinical supervision at public hospitals in Lesotho. Methods The study employed an exploratory descriptive qualitative research design to explore and describe the support provided to registered nurses during clinical supervision. Data was gathered through eight in-depth individual face-to-face interviews with participants purposefully selected from the public hospitals in Lesotho. Face-to-face interviews were recorded and transcribed verbatim for analysis. Data was analyzed by the researcher and the co-coder using thematic analysis as proposed by Braun and Clarke. Results Three themes emerged from the data; namely: nurse managers’ supervisory dimensions to facilitate healthcare quality, nurse managers’ supervisory practices to capacitate and support registered nurses and nurse managers’ challenges with clinical supervision. The findings indicate that nurse managers provide structural support to registered nurses, apply various supervisory methods and processes, and supervise nursing practices in ways that relate to patient care outcomes during clinical supervision. Conclusion Nurse managers guide registered nurses through performance monitoring, quality assurance, and resource supervision to uphold standards and policies. Supervision of registered nurses also support skill development, conflict management, and psycho-social well-being. However, challenges include addressing registered nurses’ attitudes, managing skill gaps, and overcoming nurse managers’ own knowledge limitations.
