Here we report 24 patients with nine rare and seven novel variants in the primary cilia gene C2CD3, which has previously been implicated in the ciliopathy Orofaciodigital syndrome XIV. Patients displayed an array of dental defects impacting the number, shape, and timing of tooth development. To understand the etiology underlying these defects, murine and avian models were analyzed during embryonic development. Ap2Cre;C2cd3 ex4-5 fl/fl mouse mutants showed a range of dental defects prenatally, mimicking several of the phenotypes observed in patients. Shh was upregulated in the developing upper jaw, leading to a widening of the midline, while Shh expression in the lower jaw was reduced, highlighting the context-dependent impact of cilia on hedgehog signaling. In avian mutants carrying a C2CD3 variant, talpid 2 , tooth buds were evident with SHH expression upregulated during early development in both upper and lower jaws. Cartilage defects were additionally observed in both conditional mouse knockouts and talpid 2 embryos. These changes in Shh signaling provide a mechanism to explain the phenotypes in patients and highlight the conserved role of C2CD3 in coordinating the morphogenetic potential of the jaw and patterning of the forming dentition. Given the conserved phenotypes, alterations in C2CD3-dependent ciliogenesis may have played a role in modulating Shh signaling to alter the timing and position of tooth germs across vertebrate evolution.
ne14deab1f7a7: Cooperativity of residue interactions is prevalent in proteins and plays an essential role in protein folding. However, whether cooperativity exists in intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and their assembled biomolecular condensates remains elusive. Here, we reveal the presence of residue interaction cooperativity in various IDP condensates using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations. In all these condensates, cooperative residue interactions manifest as packing between finite residue motifs (3 to 5 residues) with lifetimes three orders of magnitude longer than residue contacts. Notably, these higher-order interactions (HOIs) exhibit a significant nonadditive free energy, which originates from a local low-dielectric environment. The underlying sequence patterns like “Y-X-Q”, “D-X-R”, and “S-Y-X” are identified. Furthermore, HOIs dominate the cohesive energy of IDPs and condensates can be treated as HOI-crosslinked networks. This model can successfully reproduce experimental results of condensate physical properties, including saturation concentration, viscoelasticity, and interfacial tension.
n4b1ba5bba29c: TGF-β signaling plays a pivotal role in regulating numerous cellular processes, primarily through the Smad-dependent pathway. Disruptions of the pathway are associated with developmental disorders and life-threatening diseases, such as cancer. It has been reported that TRIM33 inactivates Smad4 signaling and also drives its own signaling responses. However, the mechanism controlling TRIM33 activity has remained unclear. In this study, we identify DCAF6 as a previously unrecognized ubiquitin ligase for TRIM33. DCAF6 targets TRIM33 at Lys850 for ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation, thus abolishing TRIM33-mediated mono-ubiquitination of Smad4. As such, DCAF6 induces dual consequences: it enhances Smad4-dependent transcriptional and growth inhibitory responses, while simultaneously eliminating TRIM33-dependent developmental responses. Conversely, DCAF6 knockout suppresses Smad4-dependent responses while amplifying TRIM33-dependent responses. Therefore, DCAF6 operates as a critical regulator in the balance of TGF-β signaling between the Smad4 and TRIM33 pathways. These insights deepen our understanding of the dynamics and fate control of TGF-β signaling and may open avenues for therapeutic approaches targeting TGF-β in diseases.
n9577f5d31a16: Diverse social, engineered, and biological systems are made up of multiple interacting dynamical components; to work properly, certain components must be carefully regulated so that their dynamics avoid instability. However, many desirable properties, like optimized computation and control, emerge close to the tipping point between stability and instability, i.e., near criticality. Claims that such dynamical systems operate near criticality have been controversial because it is difficult to assess proximity to criticality when control parameters are unknown, hard to manipulate experimentally, and fluctuating in response to changing environmental or internal conditions. Moreover, observations of system dynamics are often limited to time series measurements of one or a few components. Here we develop a temporal renormalization group theory for defining criticality for univariate time series models and an information theoretic definition of proximity to criticality that is independent of model parameterization. We apply this theory to order-n autoregressive models resulting in a data-analytic strategy for time-resolved estimates of proximity to criticality based on measured univariate time series. After benchmarking our approach on diverse ground-truth cases, we apply it to recordings of spiking activity in the mammalian brain. Our estimate of proximity to criticality predicts behavior and suggests that brain dynamics shift closer to criticality during wakefulness and shift away during deep sleep.
na01baf76d9da: Benthic suspension feeders have long been thought to depend solely on particulate organic matter (POM) for their nutritional needs. Our research, conducted in the Gulf of Aqaba (Red Sea), shows that the available concentration of planktonic carbon in the reef water is too low to meet the metabolic demands (measured through in situ oxygen uptake) of common bivalves ( Spondylus sp. and Chama pacifica ) and ascidians ( Polycarpa mytiligera and Halocynthia spinosa ). In situ measurements confirmed a concentration-dependent uptake of bulk dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and protein-like dissolved organic compounds (fDOM, analyzed via spectrofluorometry) by Spondylus sp. and P. mytiligera , suggesting that DOC uptake may balance their carbon budgets. Stable isotope (δ 13 C) mixing models indicate that reef-derived DOC (mean δ 13 C = −18.4 ± 0.7‰) emerges as the primary carbon source for bivalves (57% of their body composition), far surpassing contributions from particulate sources (26% from POC > 100 µm and 14% from POC < 100 µm). While ascidians still rely primarily on POM (60 to 71%), DOC plays an essential role as a supplementary food source (23 to 29%). These results challenge the prevailing assumption that POM is the exclusive food source for these organisms. Given the widespread presence of bivalves and ascidians in benthic habitats, our findings highlight their ability to bypass the microbial loop and directly utilize dissolved organic compounds, prompting a reevaluation of current benthic carbon budgets.
nda8a32b0a013: Dlx genes have fundamental roles in the generation, differentiation, and functions of virtually all forebrain GABAergic neurons. Here we used scRNA-Seq to identify genes that are dysregulated in Dlx1/2 conditional mutants in mouse immature CGE- and MGE-derived cortical and olfactory bulb GABAergic interneurons. Dlx1/2 -regulated genes included Cxcl14 and Nr2f2 that are important for cortical interneuron (CIN) survival. We also identified DLX2-bound putative regulatory elements (pREs) of these Dlx -regulated genes. Within the Dlx -expressing lineage, some DLX-bound pREs were specific to CINs, others appeared to be constitutively bound; the latter class having activity in mature CINs. One such pRE and its associated gene, Cxcl14 , is strongly activated by Dlx1/2 and is essential for synaptogenesis onto CINs.
n5321b89b0eeb: The transition of RNA polymerase II from initiation to elongation requires the timely exchange of many factors. Some initiation factors and elongation factors contact the same RNA polymerase II surfaces in an apparently mutually exclusive manner. For example, space occupied by the initiation factor TFIIH and elongation factor Spt4/5 (also known as DSIF) are predicted to overlap. To determine whether Spt4/5 actively displaces TFIIH, or binds only after TFIIH dissociates, labeled yeast nuclear extracts were combined with single-molecule fluorescence microscopy to observe their dynamics in real time. TFIIH categorically dissociates before Spt4/5 arrives, with a clear interval in between when neither factor is present. Therefore, Spt4/5 binding is not required to dissociate TFIIH from RNA polymerase II.
n33a89403c13a: Environmental diagnosis of schistosomiasis, a disease affecting over 250 million people globally, remains challenging, thereby limiting efficient eradication efforts. Current methods, including environmental DNA (eDNA), cannot distinguish between infectious parasite life stages present in the environment. Here, we develop and validate an environmental RNA (eRNA) approach that enables detection and quantification of Schistosoma mansoni miracidia (infective to snails) and cercariae (infective to humans) directly from water samples. We identified life stage–specific transcripts and designed ddPCR assays highly specific to S. mansoni and each life stage. Laboratory experiments demonstrate that stage-specific eRNA assays accurately detect and quantify the relative abundance of each life stage. While eRNA and eDNA assays showed similar analytical limits of detection (LOD), eRNA provided enhanced organism-level detectability due to higher target molecule availability per life stage, also resulting in longer signal persistence in water that may facilitate the detection of the highly transient free-living stages of S. mansoni in the environment, especially cercariae. Field validation at six endemic sites in Brazil confirms that eRNA outperforms eDNA and conventional snail surveys in detecting S. mansoni cercariae indicating local transmission risk to humans. By enabling living stage discrimination and improving detectability compared to eDNA, our study advances both fundamental understanding and environmental surveillance of schistosomiasis transmission, supporting elimination initiatives in affected regions.
nc15a8ed6b519: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is associated with an increase in hippocampal neurogenesis and memory benefits, but the causal mechanism is unclear. Here, we use a mouse model of Rett syndrome, a severe learning disability syndrome caused by MECP2 loss of function, to find that DBS promotes the maturation and integration of newborn dentate granule cells (DGCs) into the neural circuit. Suppressing hippocampal neurogenesis prevented DBS from improving learning and memory. Newborn methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2)-deficient DGCs in Rett syndrome mice showed attenuated development and synaptic dysfunction, but DBS rescued DGC dendritic arborization, synaptogenesis, and long-term synaptic plasticity. DBS achieves this, at least in part, by increasing the protein level and shifting the phosphorylation of potassium chloride cotransporter 2, thereby restoring the conversion of GABAergic signaling from depolarization to hyperpolarization, a process that is otherwise delayed by MeCP2 deficiency. This study pinpoints one mechanism by which chronic DBS promotes neuronal maturation and enhances memory.
n4ea7d0d92dee: The atypical cyclin-dependent kinase subfamily (CDK14–18) encompasses five related proteins with unclear function, and for which individual depletion has not demonstrated sustained therapeutic relevance. We report here that CDK16 and CDK18 compensate each other and liver cancer cells are sensitive to the concomitant inactivation of both kinases, resulting in persistent defects in DNA repair and subsequent cell death. These effects are linked to a role of CDK16/18 in regulating nucleocytoplasmatic transport through phosphorylation of nuclear pore complex components, including NUP35. Genetic ablation of Cdk16 and Cdk18 in established liver tumors driven by MYC and beta-catenin oncogenes triggers DNA damage in cancer cells without affecting adjacent normal tissue, ultimately leading to tumor regression. Collectively, these findings provide a rationale for the development of CDK16–18 inhibitors—likely targeting multiple subfamily members due to their structural similarity—as a strategy against aggressive cancers, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, where effective treatment options remain limited.
n073fd898b3b8: Conventional whole tumor cell cancer vaccines have demonstrated limited clinical success due to insufficient immunogenicity and challenges in adjuvant codelivery, despite their rich antigen repertoire and high patient-specific activity. Here, we introduce a simple, single-step approach to load immunostimulatory CpG oligodeoxynucleotides into tumor cells undergoing immunogenic cell death using an ionic liquid–containing cocktail. Results indicate that these adjuvant-loaded tumor cells (referred to as IL-Vax) enhance the uptake of cell-based vaccines by dendritic cells and their subsequent activation, leading to potent antitumor immunity. IL-Vax offered strong protection against tumor growth in a prophylactic B16F10 melanoma mouse model. Furthermore, IL-Vax synergized with PD-1 blockade to slow tumor growth and extend survival in a therapeutic model. The modularity of IL-Vax enables the loading of different cargos or cargo combinations, which may be conducive for additional tailoring of such vaccines and potentially other cell loading applications.
n07740e6e99c8: Unlike dissolved inorganic nitrogen, which is scarce in much of the tropical, subtropical, and temperate surface ocean, dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) has significant concentrations and gradients. Accordingly, the lateral transport of DON may fuel biological productivity in nutrient-depleted low-latitude surface waters. Here, we report measurements of the concentration and 15 N/ 14 N ratio (δ 15 N) of DON in surface waters over the Pacific and Atlantic basins. DON concentration is generally highest in subpolar and equatorial waters, with minima in the subtropical gyres. A δ 15 N correlation is observed between surface DON and the nitrate consumed in the surface waters, indicating in situ DON production and consumption. Samples with lower DON concentrations tend to have anomalously high DON δ 15 N, confirming net DON transport to, and consumption in, the subtropical gyres. Net local DON production or consumption appears to dominate the observed spatial variation in the DON-to-subsurface nitrate δ 15 N difference. For example, N 2 fixation tends to lower the δ 15 N of surface DON relative to subsurface nitrate mostly through encouraging DON accumulation rather than by the specific δ 15 N of the nitrogen introduced by N 2 fixation. Unique conditions appear to apply in the equatorial Atlantic, where despite high productivity, a local minimum in DON concentration and a slight elevation in DON δ 15 N suggest net DON degradation. In this phosphorus-rich, nitrogen-poor upwelling environment where low iron may restrict N 2 fixation, net decomposition of DON may supply needed recycled nitrogen to the ecosystem.
naaa9b7a7c45d: A Liouville-based framework is developed for optimizing treatment strategies in oesophageal cancer (OC) while accounting for inter-patient heterogeneity. Variability within a patient cohort is represented through uncertain initial cancer and immune cell populations, whose probability distribution is propagated by a Liouville partial differential equation while the underlying individual dynamics remains deterministic. Two optimization problems are considered. First, model parameters are estimated from population-level data using an adjoint-based projected nonlinear conjugate-gradient (NCG) method. Second, optimal time-dependent combinations of chemotherapy and immunotherapy are determined using a sequential quadratic Hamiltonian (SQH) scheme based on Pontryagin’s maximum principle (PMP). The Liouville equation is discretized using a finite-volume method designed to preserve positivity and conservation of the probability density. Numerical experiments with synthetic population data are used to demonstrate the parameter-estimation framework and the ability of the proposed optimal control strategy to determine treatment protocols that effectively modify the population-level cancer–immune response while limiting treatment exposure.
nb78f23c40146: Patience Seamount, within Australia's Huon Marine Park, hosts persistent deep-sea fish aggregations dominated by basketwork eels (Diastobranchus capensis) and orange roughy (Hoplostethus atlanticus). Using integrated hydroacoustic surveys, deep towed camera imagery and physical sampling from 2023 to 2025, we quantified the spatial and temporal dynamics of these assemblages and produced species-specific biomass estimates. Acoustic backscatter attribution followed a two-phase approach: (i) camera-derived species distributions to inform spatial apportioning of backscatter and (ii) conducting biomass-constrained sensitivity analyses applying conservative bounds on orange roughy biomass (200–850 t) informed by historical assessments. We found a large, seasonally variable basketwork eel aggregation that increased markedly from March to May, when biomass reached 3547–3557 t (approx. 2.8 million individuals), likely corresponding to spawning. Distinct habitat preferences—with basketwork eels on deeper, flatter terrain and orange roughy on steep summit slopes—improved spatial separation of backscatter in this mixed-species environment. Without biomass constraints, orange roughy estimates became implausible relative to regional stock assessments, underscoring the need for species discrimination in deep-sea acoustic analyses. Patience Seamount's protection and recovery from historical fishing provide a rare opportunity for long-term study of deep-sea ecological processes. Our methods offer a scalable, non-invasive framework for monitoring deep-sea aggregations in marine protected areas.
nf224a880847a: The identity of the extinct large crane Grus primigenia has been debated for over 150 years. Alternative interpretations suggest that such large crane remains represent extant cranes such as the sarus crane Antigone antigone, the Siberian white crane Leucogeranus leucogeranus or simply larger individuals of common crane Grus grus. Morphometrics has shown that the common crane is sexually dimorphic today with larger males and smaller females. We analysed cranes from the Late Pleistocene to Late Holocene and found that the lack of smaller female-sized craneremains suggests that G. grus may have reduced in size over time. In the present study, we successfully performed an ancient DNA analysis to assess the phylogenetic identity of 18 crane remains from the Late Pleistocene of Spain and France and the Late Holocene of Britain and Germany. All remains were identified as G. grus. These ancient cranes included individuals that were larger than modern G. grus and ones that conformed in size with common crane today. Ancient DNA-based sexing found that all the bones that were larger than those of modern males were male, while specimens the size of modern males included ancient females. This confirmed that the ancient cranes were sexually dimorphic G. grus that have become smaller since the Saxon times (884 yr BP).
n23c196eaecd7: The largest baleen whale mortality event on record, when more than 340 sei whales (Balaenoptera borealis) stranded in Chilean Patagonia during the extreme 2015 El Niño, provided a unique opportunity to reconstruct multi-year individual life histories from baleen plates. Baleens of seven females and four males were sampled to examine sex-specific foraging strategies, reproductive cycles and endocrine patterns through integrated molecular, isotopic and hormonal analyses. Sex was identified using a refined DNA amplification protocol. Patterns of δ13C and δ15N revealed significant annual oscillations, enabling estimates of baleen growth rates (15.7–20.5 cm yr−1) and retrospective timelines of up to 3.5 years. Males exhibited broader isotopic niche widths, suggesting sex-related foraging differences. Progesterone was detected in all samples, with sustained elevations in females indicating pregnancies of 7.7–10.7 months. One female exhibited two complete pregnancies recorded in baleen, enabling estimation of a 1.3-year intercalving interval. Concurrent elevations of cortisol and corticosterone were observed during pregnancy. Conceptions and births were distributed across multiple seasons, with no clear evidence of seasonal concentration. Together, these findings provide the first baleen-based reconstruction of sei whale reproductive history and endocrine variation, establishing critical baselines for assessing population resilience and informing conservation under rapid environmental change.
nbfb4b1a13c71: Universities, journals and funding bodies increasingly encourage qualitative data sharing, yet practical guidance for making interview and focus group transcripts accessible remains difficult to locate. This scoping review maps actionable strategies to overcome barriers to sharing qualitative data. The review included all sources of evidence, enabling capture of suggestions made by qualitative scholars themselves, as well as those from journals and repositories. A comprehensive search of peer-reviewed and grey literature identified 110 sources. Extracted suggestions were categorized into seven interrelated themes: confidentiality, consent, data misuse, context, external approvals, researcher distress, and time and financial constraints. These findings are consolidated into a table-based tool to guide researchers toward the most practical resources for each barrier. The review highlights the diversity and complexity of qualitative data sharing, the absence of systematic evaluation of strategies and the importance of avoiding one-size-fits-all data sharing expectations. By providing a structured, accessible resource, this work aims to support researchers in ethically, effectively and confidently sharing qualitative data, while informing funders and institutions developing open data policies.
n248710a66e54: Patent codes may lack granularity when carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) inventions combine climate and chemical engineering concepts. We evaluate term presence models on 10 603 English patent abstracts through document completion, calibration and cooperative patent classification (CPC) prefix retrieval. We compare two variational autoencoders (VAEs), a product of the experts latent Dirichlet allocation model, a unigram prior, term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF), PatentSBERTa and PaECTER. With a target masking rate of 50 per cent for positive terms, TF-IDF nearest neighbours give the best ranked completion. The direct Bernoulli VAE ranks slightly above the negative binomial to Bernoulli VAE (NB VAE), while the latter has lower expected calibration error (ECE). Conditional posterior predictive draws retain positive rank associations for document and term counts, but the NB VAE and direct Bernoulli VAE predict 1.47 and 1.63 times the observed positive count, respectively. PaECTER and the TF-IDF representation after singular value decomposition (SVD) give the strongest CPC prefix retrieval, while VAE probabilities could support inspectable term screening.
n2864cc69ed20: Many birds collect and store food for later use, a behaviour known as caching. Theoretical models predict that caching effort is concentrated in a single peak during the day, though the precise timing of that peak depends on multiple factors. We studied diurnal patterns of feeder used in a population of 50 individually marked black-capped chickadees (Poecile atricapillus) in late summer. We used total daily feeder visits (1 visit ≈ 1 sunflower seed) as a proxy for caching intensity because daily feeder visits (range 11–339 feeder visits per bird per day) often exceeded the required intake of about 45 sunflower seeds for chickadees at this time of year, consistent with a wide range of caching effort. Patterns of feeder use were always bimodal, and increases in hourly feeder visits occurred throughout the day with increased total daily feeder visits, however, the greatest relative increase in feeder visits was during midday. Post hoc analyses revealed that this population-level effect was driven by individual differences; some chickadees increased morning feeder visits with increasing total daily feeder visits, while others increased midday or end-of-day feeder visits. Future work should investigate drivers of these individual differences, including the role of interference competition.
nb10234577d82: Understanding abstract phenomena is a fundamental human need. Emerging evidence increasingly points to the multidimensionality of abstract knowledge representations, with theories emphasizing the importance of both embodied and linguistic influences. In the present paper, we argue that the strength with which embodiment is associated with abstract concepts is moderated by cultural beliefs about ontological meaning. Specifically, we predicted that self-identified spirituality—a belief system guided by an experiential approach to understanding reality—contributes to greater sensorimotor associations with abstract concepts. As hypothesized, across four studies (n = 729; in the USA and the UK), Western spiritual beliefs involved stronger sensorimotor associations for highly abstract compared to concrete concepts. Importantly, religious beliefs that conceptually overlap with spirituality did not contribute to these associations. Altogether, individual differences in belief systems guide people's conscious attendance to sensorimotor features when thinking about abstract concepts, with spiritual individuals likely feeling the meaning of words through linking abstract thought with bodily experiences.
n795435462a4c: Melanin-based pigmentation in vertebrates has often been regarded as a stable trait, inexpensive to produce and highly heritable. Accumulating evidence, however, links melanin patterns to behavioural, physiological and endocrine variation. In salmonids, eumelanin-based skin spottiness has been associated with stress responsiveness and coping style, but it remains unclear to what extent environmental challenge induces within-individual state-dependent changes in spot expression. Here, we examined whether feeding dynamics during acclimation to novelty are associated with longitudinal changes in visible skin spot density in juvenile Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), in which dark patterns are expressed through eumelanin-containing melanophores. Fish were transferred from group rearing to individual housing, inducing transient feeding suppression followed by large inter-individual variation in feeding recovery and growth. Although visible spot density declined overall, the magnitude and direction of change varied among individuals and covaried with feed intake, growth and condition factor. Individuals with higher feed intake and growth, and smaller declines in condition factor, exhibited reduced spot loss and, in some cases, increased spot density, whereas lower-performing individuals showed larger reductions. Pre-existing spot patterns predicted post-transfer performance. These findings suggest that salmonid skin spots track resource acquisition and coping capacity, consistent with regulated phenotypic plasticity in condition-associated visible pigmentation.
n224823634a2e: Perceptual biases—disproportionate sensory responses to specific stimuli—are widespread in animals and can be exploited by predators to attract prey. However, this mechanism has not been rigorously tested in carnivorous plants. We investigated whether the yellow-green traps of Drosera finlaysonii (Droseraceae) exploit hemipterans’ preference for yellow to yellow-green stimuli that strongly activate green relative to blue photoreceptors. Using multispectral imaging, we quantified trap brightness and modelled the green-to-blue photoreceptor activation ratio (G/B ratio) of hemipteran prey. We characterized the taxonomic composition of prey captured by D. finlaysonii and deployed adhesive models differing in brightness and G/B ratio. We then compared arthropod assemblages between plants and models, and taxon-specific capture numbers among models. D. finlaysonii traps were brighter and had higher G/B ratios than sympatric graminoid leaves. Hemiptera were a major prey component, although their relative abundance varied between years. Yellow models, with the highest G/B ratio, captured more hemipterans than other colour models. However, arthropod assemblages captured by D. finlaysonii differed from those captured by yellow models, with proportionally more dipterans and fewer hemipterans. Thus, a high G/B ratio may contribute to hemipteran attraction and capture but cannot alone explain the overall prey assemblage in D. finlaysonii.
nb4714bb1e580: Natural environments are generally dynamic; examples of background motion include changes in illumination and moving physical features, such as wind-blown foliage or flowing water. Experimental evidence suggests dynamic backgrounds can impede predation by masking the movement of a target, but the interaction between background motion and the movement of prey in groups has not been investigated. Dynamic backgrounds could potentially enhance the confusion effect, the phenomenon whereby locating and/or tracking a single target among similar individuals (‘distractors’) becomes less successful owing to difficulty in discriminating this target from its conspecifics. We investigated whether dynamic backgrounds contribute to the confusion effect by impeding accurate tracking of a target among distractors. We hypothesize that any effect would be greatest when the temporal properties of the background's movement match those of the moving objects. In two experiments, human surrogate ‘predators’ tracked a single target among distractors, moving unpredictably, on backgrounds that drifted coherently in a given direction. Tracking was generally poorer when backgrounds and objects moved at more closely matched speeds, probably owing to temporary masking of prey target movement and subsequent difficulty in re-locating the target among distractors. Our findings identify a role for dynamic backgrounds in defending against predation.
n49ffc4951894: Acropora palmata is a key branching coral in the Caribbean, contributing to reef complexity and providing habitat for diverse species. In recent decades, its abundance and distribution have declined, highlighting the need to better understand its ecological role. Visual surveys along linear transects in the Limones and Picudas reefs (Quintana Roo, Mexico) identified macrofaunal species associated with A. palmata and evaluated their interactions to assess habitat use. A total of 81 species were recorded, 34 of which were shared between both reefs. The recorded groups included fish, crustaceans, polychaetes, echinoderms and molluscs. Species composition was similar across both reefs, despite the particular characteristics of each reef. The structure of A. palmata was found to generate spatially heterogeneous areas that function as habitat, refuge, feeding sites and territorial spaces at the colony level. Although the colony-specific area influenced species abundance, no effect on size was detected. These findings indicate that, at the colony scale, A. palmata provides microhabitats that support diverse assemblages across different reef conditions. This suggests a lack of functional redundancy in the region: Acropora cervicornis, its only structural analogue, mainly shelters small-bodied taxa and has become even more depleted, leaving A. palmata’s habitat role without a substitute.
n0197942c3e88: Some bacterial endosymbionts of aphids can reduce mummification rates following attack by parasitoids, yet these endosymbionts can remain at a low frequency in populations even when parasitoids are present. The endosymbiont Regiella insecticola is uncommon in the major pest aphid Myzus persicae despite providing apparent protection against parasitoid attack. Here, we consider population-level effects associated with Regiella in its native M. persicae host as well as Regiella transinfected into pest Rhopalosiphum padi (oat aphids) and Diuraphis noxia (Russian wheat aphids), focusing on two parasitoids (Diaeretiella rapae, Aphidius colemani). We consider their impact not only on mummification rates but also on fecundity of non-mummified aphids that have been stung by wasps as detected by a qPCR assay to detect parasitoid DNA, with experiments simulating a single parasitoid attack event. Regiella produced a sharp decrease in mummification rates of their native and transinfected hosts, but aphids with Regiella that were stung (successful oviposition confirmed by molecular analysis) and not mummified showed low reproduction. The combination of these effects meant we did not detect major differences in the population size of infected and uninfected aphids. These results highlight the importance of considering multi-trait effects when assessing the impacts of endosymbiont infections and predicting the outcome of endosymbiont–host–parasitoid interactions.
ne03080b4ef3a: In this study, a novel environmentally friendly leveller, imidazole-pentaerythritol glycidyl ether (IMDPGE), which is free of sulfur (S) and other pollutant elements, was developed by chemical synthesis for blind-hole filling in acidic copper electroplating. The chemical structure of IMDPGE was characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry. The molecular properties of IMDPGE were investigated through quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations, and its levelling performance was predicted accordingly. The electrochemical characteristics of IMDPGE, as well as its interactions with the accelerator bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS) and the suppressor propyleneoxide (PO)-ethylene oxide (EO)-propylene oxide (PO), named PEP (EPE), were evaluated using galvanostatic potential transient measurements, cyclic voltammetry and linear scan voltammetry. The results demonstrated that IMDPGE exhibited strong polarization capability, which persisted even in the absence of SPS. Additionally, a kinetically controlled competitive adsorption existed between IMDPGE and SPS, while a synergistic inhibitory effect was observed between IMDPGE and EPE. The blind-hole filling performance of IMDPGE was verified through electroplating experiments. For the optimized EPE-SPS-IMDPGE additive system, a filling rate of 90.7% and a surface copper thickness of 7.7 µm were achieved after electroplating at a current density of 2 A dm–² for 30 minutes.
n03a804ec4b06: Mpox has transitioned from outbreak to sustained transmission in Brazil, a country with high ecological and social connectivity. We analysed the epidemiological trajectory of mpox during 2022–2025 using 14 475 laboratory-confirmed cases reported by the Brazilian Ministry of Health. The epidemic disproportionately affects men (93.0%), particularly young adults, with transmission primarily associated with networks of men who have sex with men (69.1%). A substantial burden of co-infections was identified: 47.1% of reported cases occurred in persons living with HIV and 30.8% had syphilis. Clinically, most patients presented with cutaneous manifestations (91.3%). These findings highlight the convergence of epidemiological and social determinants shaping mpox transmission in Brazil. Strengthening integrated surveillance systems and ensuring equitable, stigma-free access to prevention and care are critical to reducing transmission and mitigating the risk of broader dissemination.
nd9c60c57b6c4: Misinformation governance on short-video platforms depends on strategic interaction among online media, netizens, platforms and government regulators, but platform decisions are often treated as exogenous in two- and three-party models. Equilibrium analysis and numerical simulations identify the stable strategy profiles and the conditions under which they emerge. Under the baseline parameters, the system has a unique asymptotically stable profile. Parameter analysis shows that higher platform traffic revenue, a greater probability of insider refutation, and larger credibility and reputational losses accelerate convergence to this profile. Strict supervision can alter the transient evolutionary path and accelerate convergence under the benchmark conditions, but it is not part of the stable profile. Within the model, active platform governance and user rationality are the principal stabilizing factors, while government supervision plays a complementary role. These results provide a modelling basis for coordinating platform, user and regulatory responses to misinformation in short-video ecosystems.
n1f7f51bbb3a3: Robust zooarchaeological analysis of Pleistocene-Holocene faunal assemblages is fundamental for reconstructing past environments, species distributions, human subsistence and faunal turnovers in North America. However, faunal remains from archaeological and palaeontological sites are commonly highly fragmented or modified, often precluding morphological identification and limiting the information they can provide about faunal communities and their relationships with human populations and changing climates. Zooarchaeology by Mass Spectrometry (ZooMS) provides an effective biomolecular means of overcoming this limitation, enabling the identification of unidentifiable bone fragments, but its resolution depends on the availability of empirically validated reference datasets, which remain incomplete for North American fauna. Here, we expand the North American ZooMS reference library by characterizing and validating collagen peptide markers for 22 extant and extinct mammal taxa across four mammalian orders: Artiodactyla, Perissodactyla, Carnivora and Rodentia, integrating Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometry fingerprinting with Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry peptide sequencing to provide sequence-level validation of diagnostic peptide markers. The resulting markers enable robust family-level discrimination across a range of taxa with genus- or species-level identification possible for several groups. This expanded reference framework enhances the taxonomic resolution and applicability of ZooMS across North American faunal assemblages, supporting its use for advancing archaeological, palaeontological and conservation-related research on the continent.
n566fe52faa2f: Sociality, in particular group-living, can present many challenges to individuals and is widely thought to influence the development and evolution of cognition. We quantified the rates of two types of extragroup interactions (intergroup and interspecific interactions) in adult Western Australian magpies (Gymnorhina tibicen dorsalis) and compared these to individual performance across a battery of four cognitive tasks. We also investigated whether response to playback of intruding conspecifics (an assessment of quantity discrimination abilities) was related to intergroup interaction rate. We hypothesized that greater involvement in extragroup interactions would be positively related to cognitive performance; however, we found no support for this. We did identify a relationship between intergroup interaction rate and response to playback, with individuals involved in more intergroup interactions exhibiting a greater difference in response to one and three calling extragroup conspecifics. Our findings suggest that extragroup interactions experienced in adult life do not influence performance in food-based cognitive tasks, but research on individuals during the developmental stage is needed to rule out an effect of extragroup interactions on cognitive development.
n90ae2ca61ce3: ‘Condition’ is often used to describe the underlying state or quality of an individual and is expected to influence traits essential for fitness. Instead, they are typically inferred using measurable traits, which may capture only limited aspects of these constructs. Herein, we use structural equation modelling to integrate multiple proxy measurements, quantify the influence of underlying condition and reproductive investment on proxies and examine the relationship between condition and reproductive investment. Using Gryllus vocalis field crickets, we constructed sex-specific models to account for differences in reproductive strategies and trait expression between males and females. Both models identified proxies that were significantly influenced by condition and reproductive investment, although the strength of this influence varied across traits, suggesting that some proxies are better indicators than others. Both models also revealed significant positive relationships between condition and reproductive investment. Overall, our results demonstrate that condition positively influences reproductive investment, while revealing that commonly used proxies vary in how well they reflect these underlying constructs.
nb4d02cdcdf70: Ovarian cancer progression is driven by complex interactions among tumour, immune, stromal, metabolic and angiogenic processes. Local one-at-a-time (OAT) and global Sobol’ sensitivity analyses identified tumour growth kinetics, CAF–ECM interactions, metabolic regulation and selected hesperidin-response parameters as principal determinants of system behaviour. Although not calibrated for quantitative prediction, the proposed framework provides mechanistic insight into how hesperidin-mediated perturbations propagate through interconnected tumour–immune–stromal networks. The model should be regarded as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating platform supporting future experimental validation of hesperidin-mediated mechanisms in ovarian cancer.
n72ad65e872df: Carcasses are valuable resources to those scavengers able to access them. While some generalist foragers are poorly equipped to process carcasses themselves, they may exploit the actions of others by feeding on tissues that the latter expose or detach. Carcasses also attract opportunistic predators, which can target other smaller scavengers, as well as feeding on the carcass itself. We studied these interactions using field-based experiments in a rockpool ecosystem. First, we showed that greater numbers of small fishes and mysids were attracted to areas where scavengers, primarily hermit crabs (Pagurus bernhardus), were feeding on mussel carcass baits compared to treatments where inaccessible carcasses or no-carcass controls were presented. We termed these secondary scavengers, since we did not see them feeding on the carcass directly. Second, we saw predators attack scavengers more frequently in trials where carcasses were present than where they were absent. They also approached stimulus chambers containing aggregations of hermit crabs more often than empty controls. Nonetheless, predator interactions were, overall, infrequent. For these smaller scavengers, carcass-foraging may be a trade-off between access to a sizeable food resource and competition, and sometimes heightened predation risk, from larger scavengers.
n996179ca2d47: Body dissatisfaction is a key risk factor for psychiatric illnesses and is a modifiable target. Previous gaze-tracking research suggests that body dissatisfaction is related to greater attentional bias towards lower-weight bodies. Here, we aimed to partially replicate and extend previous work to verify this association by using realistic body stimuli and a validated scale of body dissatisfaction. Sixty, mostly young, women from the general population underwent eye-tracking while viewing picture pairs of women's bodies morphed to lower and higher weights. Attentional bias was measured as percentage fixation duration, fixation count and first fixations on lower-weight compared to higher-weight bodies. There was weak evidence that all women fixated for longer on lower-weight bodies, and that participants with higher body dissatisfaction spent less time fixating on lower-weight bodies, contrary to our hypotheses and to previous findings, but this effect was not robust to adjustment for age and body mass index. This lack of replication suggests this association is not robust in non-clinical populations. Instead, an overall bias towards lower-weight bodies could contribute to higher levels of body dissatisfaction and risk of mental health problems in younger women. Future studies measuring attentional biases in realistic settings and in clinical populations with eating disorder symptoms are needed.
n99ebd3ab44f8: Temminck's ground pangolin is one of Africa's most threatened mammals, yet little is known about its skeletal biology. Extensive skeletal reinforcement occurs throughout the limbs, although elements employ distinct osteohistological patterns. Comparison with the aardvark reveals alternative pathways of skeletal reinforcement, with ground pangolins showing relatively greater secondary remodelling in the hind limb. Ground pangolins are further distinguished by abundant, incompletely infilled resorption cavities extending into the middle and outer cortex, suggesting an unusual pattern of intracortical remodelling. The exceptionally low basal metabolic rate of S. temminckii may contribute to these patterns, although this relationship remains to be tested. These findings provide new insights into the skeletal biology of this poorly studied mammal.
nc258c30972d9: Effective management of threatened and migratory species requires monitoring of critical behaviours, such as foraging. Passive acoustic monitoring can provide cost-effective, long-term observations on the relative abundance of vocal animals across large spatial scales. However, linking specific sounds to behavioural contexts can be challenging, especially for cryptic and aquatic species. This study combined passive acoustic and biologging data to explore whether observed periods of greater nocturnal than diurnal song production were linked to feeding by eastern Indian Ocean pygmy blue whales, Balaenoptera musculus brevicauda. The proportion of time available for singing was modelled as a function of geographical region, diel period and the presence or absence of feeding dives with generalized linear mixed models, based on 130.1 days of diving data. Top-ranked models indicated less time was available for singing during diurnal feeding periods compared to nocturnal feeding periods and non-feeding periods during the day and night. These findings suggest that diurnal feeding by pygmy blue whales reduces the time available for song production. Therefore, greater nocturnal than diurnal song production may provide an acoustic indicator of population-level feeding activity for pygmy blue whales between the Perth Canyon and offshore of the northwest shelf of Western Australia.
nf2f486392fc8: Preregistration—the prospective registration of hypotheses, methods and analyses plans—is a promising tool in promoting transparency, rigour and reproducibility in science. Within a larger cross-sectional mixed-methods project, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 Swiss-based researchers involved in animal research and thematically analysed independently by two researchers. Preregistration was described as uncommon in animal research, with views varying by prior experience. Researchers with preregistration experience reported more positive views, whereas those without were more critical. Main barriers included administrative burden, time constraints, limited flexibility and perceived incompatibility with exploratory research. Reported benefits comprised improved study planning, adherence to good research practices and increased transparency. Suggestions to improve uptake involved training, institutional support, integration with the existing authorization procedure and maintaining voluntary participation. Preregistration in animal research remains uncommon and is shaped by prior experience. Addressing barriers through training, institutional support and structural integration may broaden its adoption.
na8ee134559a9: We study how passive virtual observation of cyber-physical systems (CPS) can affect human trust in those systems. We perform this study via a newly developed novel web application that enables researchers to show pre-recorded or live video feeds to groups of users in a synchronized fashion. Users are able to provide real-time feedback on these videos via affect buttons and a free-form chat interface. We evaluate our application via a quantitative user study (N≈80) involving videos of CPS, such as autonomous vehicles (AVs), performing positively or negatively. Using data collected from user responses in the application, as well as customized survey instruments assessing different facets of trust, we find that human trust in CPS can be affected by remotely observing the behaviour of such systems—without ever encountering them in person.
n07f2fe92e637: The Neotropical lizard Ameiva ameiva is widespread in Brazil, occurring in contrasting climatic regimes that can shape its reproductive tactics. Males produced sperm year-round, and most individuals remained in recrudescence or spermiogenesis. Mating coincided with vitellogenesis and ovulation in all populations, and the presence of mating plugs and stored sperm may indicate that females can produce multiple clutches per reproductive season. Together, these patterns show that A. ameiva exhibits a continuous reproductive cycle at the individual level but a seasonal, semi-synchronous cycle at the population level. Temporal differences among populations, particularly in the timing of vitellogenesis and mating, thus demonstrate reproductive plasticity that may contribute to the species's ability to persist across diverse and changing environments.
n137fcc39c61e: Tsetse flies exhibit varying host preferences when seeking blood meals. Laboratory two-choice olfactometer assays showed dose-dependent attraction to all tested compounds, with significantly more flies choosing treatment arms than control arms (p < 0.05). Field responses to geosmin and CO2 were validated using a randomized Latin square design, in which traps baited with either odour captured significantly more tsetse flies than unbaited control traps (p < 0.05). Incorporating these compounds into existing odour-bait systems could improve the effectiveness of environmentally friendly and cost-effective tsetse control strategies.
ne50cfef3256b: Spinosaurid theropods exhibited a relatively widespread distribution during the Cretaceous Period; however, biogeographical analyses have been limited, largely owing to their fragmentary nature and uncertainties in spinosaurid phylogeny. Within Spinosauridae, we find at least two distinct dispersals from Europe into Africa and South America, as well as at least one dispersal from Europe into Asia. Based on existing climate model data, spinosaurids generally appear to occur in high mean annual temperature semi-aquatic environments (approx. 26.1–33.1°C) with relatively minimal seasonal variation (approx. ±8.46°C), which may have influenced their dispersal capability, as these preferences appearmore constrained compared with those of other medium-to-large theropods. These results imply a more limited biogeographical distribution for Spinosauridae compared with other clades, which may be owing to climatic dispersal barriers and environmental factors.
naade16d97780: Casein kinase 1δ (CK1δ) is a ubiquitously expressed kinase involved in diverse cellular processes, including cell-cycle regulation. CK1δ activity is attenuated by (auto)phosphorylation. However, inhibitory phosphorylation is efficiently opposed by cellular phosphatases as CK1δ accumulates in its hypophosphorylated, active state. CK1δ is a target of the nuclear ubiquitin ligase APC/C-CDH1, yet the kinase is apparently stable. Thus, the physiological relevance of CK1δ (auto)phosphorylation, autoinhibition, and regulated turnover has remained unclear. Previously, we showed that CK1δ is dynamically regulated in a manner that is dependent on kinase activity, subcellular localization, and interaction with its binding partners, such as PER2 (Serrano et al., 2026). Here, we show that CK1δ activity and abundance are additionally coordinated in a cell cycle-dependent manner. During G1, assembled CK1δ kinase is stable while free active kinase is degraded. In S phase, unassembled CK1δ seems to be no longer degraded, likely to support functions in DNA damage signaling. Upon mitotic entry, the downregulation of phosphatases promotes CK1δ (auto)phosphorylation and consequent autoinhibition, thereby preserving a pool of kinase to rapidly re-establish the post-mitotic steady state.
necfe2bc4f973: In the mature neocortex, functionally distinct areas are built by the same archetypes of neurons, but depending on the area, these neurons and their synapses are engaged in very different functions, ranging from lower-order processing of sensory information to higher-order associations and cognitive functions. Mature synapses in PFC operated with loose microdomain coupling, as opposed to tight nanodomain coupling in S1. These differences were associated with significant differences in synaptic timing, efficacy, and plasticity between areas. Our data suggest that the mature neocortex uses tuning of synaptic topographies to specialize seemingly identical types of neurons for their required function. They suggest that microdomain coupling in pyramidal neuron synapses could be a presynaptic structure-function correlate of higher-order neocortical functions.
n24682e4edfe3: The cost of expressing unnecessary genes on growth has been explained at the population level through balanced growth assumptions. However, due to the high degree of stochasticity in growth and gene regulation, it remains unclear how classical growth laws derived from bulk measurements manifest at the level of individual cells. For example, flagellar gene expression, one of the most energy-intensive processes in Escherichia coli, is typically associated with reduced growth rates in bulk measurements. By contrast, we find at the single-cell level that a strikingly opposite behavior coexists: flagellar gene activity is associated with an increase in growth rate. We show that this apparent contradiction, reminiscent of Simpson’s paradox, results from examining in each cell instantaneous growth and gene expression without indiscriminately aggregating the single-cell data like in bulk measurements. We attribute this unrecognized behavior to out-of-balance growth boosts that temporarily offset the burden of flagellum production, likely driven by a surplus of growth factors inherited across cell division. Furthermore, we show that this non-intuitive relationship between growth and gene expression at the single-cell level is general, as we observe similar effects with synthetic systems driving the expression of fluorescent proteins downstream of constitutive promoters. Finally, we use a computational model to show that the inheritance of parental growth factors can explain the apparent contradiction and constitutes a general mechanism for mitigating the short-term cost of nonessential and biosynthetically demanding genes in the single cell.
na685753bd4a5: Central questions of animal behavior are how individual phenotypes shape and how individual phenotypes are shaped by dominance hierarchies. To test this, we created 30 replicates of juvenile clownfish, each comprising a size-matched pair housed together, and a solitary size-matched individual housed separately. Our results show that an individual’s social context shapes its growth trajectory through coordinated changes in feeding behavior, agonistic behaviors, and gene expression. Individuals emerging as dominant within pairs grew twice as much compared to those emerging as subordinates, while subordinate and solitary individuals showed comparable growth. Initially, paired individuals consumed more food per capita than solitary individuals, but this difference declined as size hierarchies became established. Agonistic behaviors also decreased over time among paired individuals as size differences emerged. Transcriptomic analyses revealed upregulation of conserved vertebrate growth pathways and ossification-related genes, and downregulation of satiety-associated genes, in dominant individuals compared to subordinates and solitaries. Here, we identify associations between changes in gene expression, growth, and feeding behavior regulation that reinforce social role differentiation during dominance hierarchy formation in clownfish. Our findings lay the foundation for a broader framework to explore the mechanisms underpinning strategic growth in social vertebrates.
n0b7eabc0a9bc: Bacterial cell division relies on precise peptidoglycan (PG) remodeling, a process orchestrated by the FtsEX complex. Upon EnvC binding, ATPase activity markedly increases. High-resolution structures of EcoFtsEX, both in the presence and absence of EnvC, reveal a symmetrical conformation of EcoFtsEX capable of accommodating the inherent asymmetry of EnvC, mediated by flexible loops within the periplasmic domain. Our negative-staining imaging showcases an elongated EcoFtsEX/EnvC/AmiB complex reminiscent of the PaeFtsEX system. These findings collectively provide intricate insights into the regulation of PG cleavage by FtsEX in E. coli—a pivotal model system used in pilot genetic studies, suggesting a conserved mechanism for precise hydrolase activation in bacteria.
n1cde861dec55: Low-intensity transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) is a promising non-invasive technique for brain stimulation and focal neuromodulation. In initial exploratory analyses with univariate tests, we find that parameters, such as the intensity and continuity of stimulation (duty cycle, DC) show statistical trends towards likely TUS neural enhancement or suppression of function. Machine-learning analyses were limited by the currently small sample size. Given that human TUS sample sizes are expected to increase, predictability on the directionality of TUS effects could improve if a database is available. Therefore, we establish an inTUS database and resource for the systematic reporting of TUS parameters and outcomes to assist in greater precision in TUS use for brain stimulation and neuromodulation. The paper concludes with a selective review of human clinical TUS studies illustrating how hypotheses on the directionality of TUS effects could be developed for empirical testing in the intended clinical application, not limited to the examples provided.
n30b10dc3afc5: Mutations of EIF2AK4, which encodes the eIF2α kinase GCN2, cause a severe inherited form of pulmonary hypertension called pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD). Unlike previously described GCN2 activators, one of these molecules activated GCN2 independently of GCN1. Modelling supported by structure activity screens suggested it binds within the ATP pocket of GCN2, but unlike existing ligands does not protrude inward into the allosteric pocket or outward into the solvent. This overcomes a key requirement of other GCN2 activators.
n33e898a8ad96: Two types of osteoblasts are required to assemble the zebrafish embryonic skeleton: classical osteoblasts homologous to the mammalian cell and notochord sheath cells which serve as non-classical osteoblasts. Here, using a newly generated transgenic line, we isolate classical and non-classical osteoblasts from zebrafish embryos and performed both assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (ATAC)-seq and RNA-seq. We analysed results independently and integratively to understand those chromatin dynamics and accompanying transcriptomic changes that occur in different skeletal cell types. We show that although Dlx family factors are playing important roles in classical osteoblast regulation, Hox family factors are involved in governing spinal ossification via non-classical osteoblasts. We further present a resource-driven analysis of the entpd5a promoter, experimentally validating the ATAC-seq dataset and proposing mechanisms of regulating the complex entpd5a expression pattern during zebrafish osteogenesis. Our results thus provide a necessary comprehensive resource for the field of bone development and indicate spatio-temporally regulated promoter/enhancer interactions taking place in the entpd5a locus.
nfb8960c5450b: The most widespread animal life cycle includes a planktonic larval stage that is environmentally induced to settle and rapidly metamorphose into a benthic juvenile. Here, using the sponge Amphimedon queenslandica, we integrate time-resolved transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility profiling across larval competence, settlement, and the first hours of metamorphosis. We show that diminishing light at sunset is associated with extensive chromatin remodelling in swimming larvae prior to settlement despite relatively modest changes in gene expression. Upon environmental induction by a coralline alga, metamorphosis is accompanied by the rapid and transient activation of a large suite of deeply conserved transcription factors (TFs), including AP-1/bZIP family members, whose binding motifs are enriched in newly accessible regulatory regions near differentially expressed genes. Larvae prevented from experiencing sunset by constant light fail to settle and instead adopt an alternative transcriptional and chromatin state characterised by widespread loss of accessibility and repression of competence-associated TFs, including the circadian regulator CLOCK and other bHLH-PAS factors. These observations support a model in which light-entrained transcriptional activity establishes an anticipatory, permissive chromatin landscape that enables immediate and coordinated transcriptional reprogramming upon environmental induction. We propose that such chromatin priming may represent a broadly deployed regulatory strategy underlying the speed and robustness of metamorphosis in biphasic animal life cycles.
ne937d3f2afc6: Mosquito-borne virus transmission is increasing globally. Testing of pooled mosquitoes via RT-qPCR is often used to infer infection prevalence; however, these data are often binarised and ignore semi-quantitative cycle threshold (Ct values) that may provide valuable information on virus kinetics, mosquito infectiousness, and ultimately human risk. West Nile virus (WNV) is a globally distributed arbovirus and endemic to the United States. In this study, we analysed pooled Ct values from retrospective mosquito surveillance and found substantial variation that could not be explained by laboratory factors alone. To understand how underlying viral load and epidemiological dynamics might explain this variation, we developed a multi-scale model linking pooled Ct values to heterogeneous within-host viral kinetics in mosquitoes and birds and seasonal transmission dynamics. Our modelling suggests that Ct values from positive pools might reflect a mixture of potentially infectious and non-infectious mosquitoes, indicating that a substantial proportion of PCR-positive mosquitoes might not contribute to transmission. We then developed a method to estimate mosquito infection prevalence using only pooled Ct values that distinguishes infectious from non-infectious prevalence. Estimates of overall prevalence were comparable to standard methods using binarised data and remained accurate at higher prevalences where standard approaches fail. Overall, these findings demonstrate that entomological viral load data reflect biologically meaningful variation in mosquito infection status that is lost through binarisation. Accounting for heterogeneous mosquito viral kinetics can improve interpretation of surveillance data and estimates of transmission risk, with implications for arbovirus surveillance beyond WNV.
na9b5be8accd9: The brain is one of the most complex animal organs, and the development of the many different neuron types remains enigmatic. A set of brain-specific transcription factors is involved in brain patterning, but their specific contributions mostly remain to be elucidated, including foxQ2II. This transcription factor is conserved in anterior neuroectodermal patterning of most animals, while it has been lost from vertebrates. The contribution of foxQ2II-positive neurons to the adult brain has remained enigmatic. Here, we use our enhancer trap, immunostainings, and our newly established beetle brainbow system to categorize Tc-foxQ2II-positive neurons into nine clusters with different projection patterns. All clusters contain neurons with the fast-activating neurotransmitters acetylcholine and glutamate, while no Tc-foxQ2II-positive neuron is GABA-ergic or serotonin-positive. Interestingly, we found that many dopaminergic neurons were Tc-foxQ2II positive and homologize them with dopaminergic neurons of the PPL2c, PPM1, and PPL1 cluster described in the Drosophila brain. Our results show that Tc-foxQ2II marks subsets of fast-acting interneurons contributing to the higher-order brain centers mushroom bodies and central complex. Taken together, our work expands the known functional range of foxQ2 genes from sensory and neurosecretory cell specification to interneurons involved in the function of higher-order brain centers.
nb45012d98ac2: Nutrient resorption is a key plant strategy for nutrient conservation, yet whether it responds plastically to non-nutrient stressors such as salinity remains unresolved. Against this backdrop of confirmed stress, we found that nutrient resorption efficiency (NuRE) remained largely unaffected by salinity. Instead, NuRE was strongly correlated with phylogeographic lineage, ecotype, and latitude of origin, demonstrating evolutionary canalization rather than short-term acclimation. Element-specific regulatory patterns were also evident: while phosphorus resorption followed concentration-dependent control regardless of stress, nitrogen control was disrupted under salinity, and potassium resorption showed no such dependence. Our findings reveal that intraspecific variation in nutrient resorption is predominantly shaped by historical adaptation and geographic context, not by plasticity to salinity. This genetic canalization of a key functional trait implies that predictions of nutrient cycling under global change must account for the phylogeographic composition of plant populations.
n3e98ebe5bbd3: As developing neural circuits become functional, they undergo a phase of heightened plasticity that facilitates network tuning in response to intrinsic and/or extrinsic stimuli. These developmental windows are termed critical periods (CPs) because perturbations during but not outside the CP can lead to lasting changes, such as the formation of sub-optimal or unstable networks. How separate but connected elements within a network might respond differently to a CP perturbation is not well understood. To study this, we used the locomotor network of the Drosophila larva as a model and heat stress as a CP stimulus that has ecological relevance. n655877e57217: Invasive exotic arthropods and weeds pose a growing threat to biodiversity, food security, and the functioning of whole ecosystems, resulting in significant socioeconomic and ecological impacts. Classical biological control—the importation of specialist natural enemies from the native range—can lead to long-term, sustainable pest suppression, but it is typically implemented reactively after the invasive species is established and is causing significant negative impacts. Proactive biological control offers an anticipatory approach, developing biological control agents before or shortly after establishment and enabling rapid response to new incursions.
